paragraphs.en: First two hours, now three hours – this is how far in advance authorities are recommending people show up to catch a domestic flight, at least at some major U.S. airports with increasingly massive security lines.
paragraphs.zh: 起初是提前两小时，现在是提前三小时——这是有关部门建议人们乘坐国内航班时提前到达机场的时间；至少在美国一些主要机场是如此，那里的安检队伍正变得越来越庞大。

paragraphs.en: Americans are willing to tolerate time-consuming security procedures in return for increased safety. The crash of EgyptAir Flight 804, which terrorists may have downed over the Mediterranean Sea, provides another tragic reminder of why. But demanding too much of air travelers or providing too little security in return undermines public support for the process. And it should: Wasted time is a drag on Americans’ economic and private lives, not to mention infuriating.
paragraphs.zh: 美国人愿意忍受耗时的安检程序，以换取更高的安全性。埃及航空804航班在地中海上空失事，可能是恐怖分子所为，这场悲剧再次提醒了人们其中的原因。但是，对航空旅客要求过多，或相应提供的安全保障过少，都会削弱公众对安检流程的支持。理应如此：浪费时间拖累了美国人的经济活动和私人生活，更不用说这还令人恼火。

paragraphs.en: Last year, the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) found in a secret check that undercover investigators were able to sneak weapons – both fake and real – past airport security nearly every time they tried. Enhanced security measures since then, combined with a rise in airline travel due to the improving economy and low oil prices, have resulted in long waits at major airports such as Chicago’s O’Hare International. It is not yet clear how much more effective airline security has become – but the lines are obvious.
paragraphs.zh: 去年，美国运输安全管理局在一次秘密检查中发现，便衣调查员几乎每次尝试，都能将真假武器偷偷带过机场安检。此后加强的安检措施，加上经济好转和油价低廉带来的航空出行增长，使芝加哥奥黑尔国际机场等主要机场出现了漫长的等候队伍。航空安检究竟变得有效了多少，目前尚不清楚——但排起的长队却一目了然。

paragraphs.en: Part of the issue is that the government did not anticipate the steep increase in airline travel, so the TSA is now rushing to get new screeners on the line. Part of the issue is that airports have only so much room for screening lanes. Another factor may be that more people are trying to overpack their carry-on bags to avoid checked-baggage fees, though the airlines strongly dispute this.
paragraphs.zh: 部分原因在于，政府没有预料到航空出行会急剧增长，因此运输安全管理局现在正匆忙安排新的安检员上岗。另一个原因在于，机场能用来设置安检通道的空间毕竟有限。还有一个因素可能是，越来越多人为了逃避托运行李费，试图往随身行李里塞入过多物品，尽管航空公司坚决否认这一说法。

paragraphs.en: There is one step the TSA could take that would not require remodeling airports or rushing to hire: Enroll more people in the PreCheck program. PreCheck is supposed to be a win-win for travelers and the TSA. Passengers who pass a background check are eligible to use expedited screening lanes. This allows the TSA to focus on travelers who are higher risk, saving time for everyone involved. The TSA wants to enroll 25 million people in PreCheck.
paragraphs.zh: 运输安全管理局可以采取一项既不需要改建机场、也不需要仓促招聘的措施：让更多人加入“预先安检”计划。该计划原本应该使旅客和运输安全管理局双赢。通过背景审查的乘客，有资格使用快速安检通道。这样，运输安全管理局就能将精力集中于风险更高的旅客，从而节省所有相关人员的时间。该局希望有2500万人加入预先安检计划。

paragraphs.en: It has not gotten anywhere close to that, and one big reason is sticker shock: Passengers must pay $85 every five years to process their background checks. Since the beginning, this price tag has been PreCheck’s fatal flaw. Upcoming reforms might bring the price to a more reasonable level. But Congress should look into doing so directly, by helping to finance PreCheck enrollment or to cut costs in other ways.
paragraphs.zh: 目前的参与人数远未接近这一目标，一个重要原因是费用让人望而却步：乘客每五年必须支付85美元，用于办理背景审查。从一开始，这一价格就是预先安检计划的致命弱点。即将出台的改革或许会把费用降到更合理的水平。但国会应研究如何直接实现这一点，例如资助人们加入预先安检计划，或以其他方式降低成本。

paragraphs.en: The TSA cannot continue diverting resources into underused PreCheck lanes while most of the traveling public suffers in unnecessary lines. It is long past time to make the program work.
paragraphs.zh: 当大多数出行公众还在忍受不必要的排队时，运输安全管理局不能继续把资源投入使用不足的预先安检通道。早就应该让这一计划真正发挥作用了。
